items.sentence_raw: But is this effect really due to a mood change caused by the heat?
Some scientists argue that trouble starts more often in hot weather merely because there are more people in the street when the weather is good.
Psychologists have also studied how being cold affects performance.
Researchers compared divers working in icy cold water at 5°C with others in water at 20°C (about swimming pool temperature).
The colder water made the divers worse at simple arithmetic and other mental tasks.
But significantly, their performance was impaired as soon as they were put into the cold water - before their bodies had time to cool down.
items.explain: Q26: The passage says the divers' performance was *'impaired as soon as they were put into the cold water'* — but importantly, this happened *'before their bodies had time to cool down'*. This means the cold did not directly slow their brain, but the *'feeling of cold distracted the divers from their tasks'*. **'Distracted'** means they were **less able to concentrate**. So the answer is **A**.

items.explain: Q33: The passage states *'The amount of melatonin falls with greater exposure to daylight'*. If melatonin falls with more daylight, it must increase when daylight decreases — for example, at certain times of the year. So the statement is **TRUE**.
